metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 2–5% for the first 5–7 days.
- After a price spike (e.g., >45), model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward; apply a downward bias of 1–3% for the next 3–5 days post-spike.
- When sentiment history is flat (all 0.00), model exhibits high volatility and overconfidence; dampen forecast variance by 15–20% and anchor to recent 7-day moving average.
- Mean reversion is strong in the final 5–7 days of the forecast horizon; adjust last 5–7 days downward by 1–3% if true outcome shows downward trend.
- If true outcome drops below 40 after a spike, model often fails to recognize the reversal; add a 2–5% downward correction to the final 3–5 days of forecast.
- Avoid forecasting sharp upward moves after a 30-day low; if true outcome shows a 30-day low, cap forecast at 10–15% below the low for next 5 days.
